A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same DIR research work, with complete main text and Appendices A-D. Text extraction and visual comparison support assessment of the equations, figures, tables and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original reward-model and PPO/DPO experiments covering length, sycophancy, formatting and concurrent biases, with numerical results and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and supplementary experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: As written, the optimization procedure changes substantially: Algorithm 1 negates both the estimator loss in line 6 and the debiasing loss in line 10 while retaining gradient descent. Equation 12 likewise changes LDebiasing from positive to negative CLUB. These edits reverse the affected gradient contributions; they do not establish that the reported experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Training datasets, evaluation benchmarks and task coverage are unchanged, including length, sycophancy, formatting and concurrent-bias scenarios, PPO/DPO evaluations and all appendix benchmarks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments. Examples include Skywork, PoE, LP, ALBM and InfoRM for length-related comparisons; BT and InfoRM for sycophancy; BT, BT† and FD for formatting; and vanilla DPO and DPO+LC.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and Appendix B retain the same reported data construction, sample sizes, model backbones, training budgets, evaluation metrics, few-shot settings and judging procedures. No experimental-setting revision accompanies the method's loss-sign edits.

E4.justification: The contamination stress tests, concurrent-bias experiments, representation and coefficient ablations, PPO training analysis, computational-cost analysis and Appendix D case study are unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or newly introduced uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: All reported numerical and qualitative results are retained, including the appendices. For example, Table 1 retains DIR average accuracies of 66.20 and 59.25, and Figure 2 retains its length-reward Pearson correlation of 0.468.

T1.justification: Equation 12 locally revises the formal definition of LDebiasing from ICLUB to -ICLUB. The bounds, assumptions and Appendix A proofs remain unchanged. This is not equivalent notation: the new definition conflicts with the retained argument that minimizing this loss minimizes an upper bound on bias information.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about information-theoretic debiasing, handling nonlinear and multiple biases, and improving reward-model and downstream alignment performance.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, interpretations of experimental results and discussions of debiasing trade-offs are unchanged. No explanation or qualification reconciles the revised loss signs with the retained mutual-information minimization rationale.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, hyperparameters, resource measurements, training-framework information, the Appendix C judging prompt and code-access information remain unchanged. The substantive loss revisions are assessed under M1 and T1.

R1.justification: Cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including comparisons with Pearson-based debiasing, InfoRM and causal approaches. The added conference-publication note does not revise the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v2 corrects 'recongized' to 'recognized', specifies the Shenzhen affiliation and adds an ICLR 2026 publication note. Section organization and the substantive narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The first-page branding changes from Alibaba Qwen Applications Business Group to QWEN BUSINESS UNIT, with limited reflow and a publication footer. All six numbered figures and twelve tables retain their displays, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: Algorithm 1's negative log-likelihood corrects the estimator's descent direction, but negating the debiasing loss makes the retained positive-weight minimization favor increasing CLUB, contrary to Equation 8 and Appendix A.2. These consequential benefits and harms coexist. The unchanged experiments do not identify which sign convention was implemented, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
